person.intro: I build complete products — refined interfaces, Android and TV apps, secure real-time APIs and cloud deployments. Co-creator of Rescuen, a personal-safety app live on Google Play.
about: I'm a final-year B.Tech Information Technology student at Bengal College of Engineering and Technology, Durgapur (Class of 2027) — and a developer who loves shipping things end to end: the interface, the mobile client, the API, the database and the deployment.

I co-built and launched Rescuen on the Google Play Store, where I owned the Android app — React Native with custom Kotlin native modules for lock-screen SOS. Since then I've built a verified campus network with WebRTC live video, an offline-capable UPI engine on Android StrongBox and Go, a Fire TV storytelling app on Amazon Bedrock, and AI products on Angular, React and Next.js.

Security, performance and accessibility matter to me as much as looks — rate limits, CSP, tests and Lighthouse scores are part of “done”. I'm looking for SDE and full-stack internships and 2027 new-grad roles where I can ship real features and learn from great engineers.
person.relocation: Open to relocate anywhere in India (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram/Noida, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata) or work remotely
person.availability: Available now for internships (full-time or part-time, remote or on-site); graduating in June 2027 for full-time SDE roles

projects.name: Rescuen
projects.role: Co-creator & Android lead — I built the Android app; my teammate owned the backend and cloud.
projects.summary: A community-powered emergency app: one hold of the SOS button alerts family, the police and every Rescuen user within 1 km — while recording evidence, even with the screen locked.
highlights: One-tap (hold) SOS — SMS to family and emergency services (112), plus instant FCM alerts to nearby Rescuen users.
1 km community radar built on geohash proximity queries.
Live location through an Android foreground service, so SOS keeps running with the screen off.
Follow-Me safe-journey mode — a dead-man's switch asks “Are you safe?” on unexpected stops and escalates to SOS.
PIN-locked Evidence Vault recording front and rear camera video with audio to owner-only cloud storage.
Gemini-powered safety assistant with function calling to guide users and trigger SOS.
Custom Kotlin native module for triple volume-key SOS and lock-screen wake, bridged into React Native.
Google Sign-In and phone-OTP onboarding, with the UI in six Indian languages.

projects.name: College Campus
projects.tagline: A verified network for Indian campuses.
projects.kind: Full-stack social platform · Web, Android & iOS
projects.summary: A LinkedIn-style network where verified students and faculty share posts, reels and stories, chat in real time, go live and find placements — on web, Android and iOS from one React codebase.
highlights: Typo-tolerant search across people, colleges, posts and hashtags using trigram similarity.
One authenticated WebSocket channel for direct messages (typing indicators, read receipts), notifications and live chat.
Go live from the phone camera over peer-to-peer WebRTC — viewers join, chat and send hearts in real time.
Document-based verification: admins review ID proofs through private, expiring links in a moderation console.
Security: bcrypt, revocable JWT sessions, Google sign-in, rate limits and lockouts, Helmet CSP/HSTS, a CORS allow-list and byte-level upload checks.
In-memory TTL cache for hot reads, Winston logging and Sentry error monitoring.
Docker Compose (API + Nginx), Kubernetes manifests (Deployment, Service, Ingress, PVC), AWS S3 media and Capacitor builds for Android and iOS.

architecture.note: Docker Compose · Kubernetes manifests · peer-to-peer WebRTC live video

projects.name: Fortress UPI
projects.summary: A UPI app built on hardware-rooted trust: every API call, offline note and receipt is signed inside Android StrongBox / TEE or the iOS Secure Enclave, and pre-funded notes move phone-to-phone over BLE or NFC — settling automatically when either phone reconnects.
highlights: Hardware ECDSA P-256 keys in StrongBox / TEE; offline notes are backed by single-use keys (setMaxUsageCount(1)).
FOP/1 offline protocol: ephemeral ECDH handshake, AES-256-GCM payloads and signed receipts over BLE or NFC.
Go stdlib-only microservices — core ledger, identity, payments, offline-mesh and security gateway — with nonce de-duplication and settlement.
Cross-language golden test vectors keep the Go, Kotlin and Swift encoders byte-identical.
Distroless containers, Kubernetes (PSA restricted, KEDA, NetworkPolicies), a Kong gateway and zero-trust, SHA-pinned CI with SAST, secret, CVE and IaC gates.
Pearl & Midnight design system with measured contrast, plus an interactive web preview of every screen.

architecture.note: Settles automatically when either phone reconnects · p99 < 15 ms load gate

projects.name: Storyloom
projects.tagline: Family stories, woven together — on Fire TV.
projects.kind: Fire TV app · Multi-agent generative AI
projects.role: Team of two — I owned product, the backend, the AI engine and the cloud infrastructure; Jayashree Mondal built the frontend and UI design.
projects.summary: A 10-foot Amazon Fire TV app where a family co-creates an original illustrated, narrated story: phones join by QR, a child's paper drawing becomes the hero, and everyone votes on what happens next.
highlights: Multi-agent story engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Strands agents — Director (Amazon Nova 2 Lite), Guardian, Illustrator, Narrator and Hero vision.
Stability AI on Bedrock turns a child's sketch into storybook art that keeps the child's own lines.
Amazon Polly narration with word-by-word read-along timing for early literacy.
Family vote at the story's fork — on phones or the Fire TV remote — with D-pad spatial navigation.
Kid-safe by design: Bedrock Guardrails on every input and output, Rekognition screening, EXIF stripping, CloudFront signed URLs and 24-hour photo deletion.
Everything as code with AWS CDK: API Gateway (HTTP + WebSocket), Lambda, DynamoDB, S3 and AgentCore Memory.

architecture.note: DynamoDB · S3 · CloudFront signed URLs · AgentCore Memory · AWS CDK

projects.name: Vitrine
projects.summary: Type a product name and category and get an AI-written title, description and SEO keywords on six luxury card templates — editable, undoable and exportable as PNG, JSON or HTML.
highlights: Angular 22 with standalone components, signals, zoneless change detection and prerendered public pages.
One Hono API deployed to both Vercel and Netlify Functions — Groq first, automatic Gemini fallback, strict zod-validated JSON.
Prompt-injection-safe design: user input is serialised inside escaped data blocks and AI output is stripped and rendered only as text.
“Ask Kabir” support assistant grounded in the Help Center with BM25 retrieval, sources and a redaction filter.
Human support tickets by email with branded confirmations, per-IP and per-recipient rate limits and a honeypot.
Firebase Auth + Firestore with owner-only rules (16 rules tests), Playwright e2e on five browsers and WCAG 2.1 AA checks with axe-core.
Brand Kit, undo/redo signal store, command palette, PWA with an offline page and light, dark and OLED themes.

projects.name: Cachet
projects.summary: Write private notes and share them with links that expire, unlock with a key or vanish after a single view — with view counts that stay accurate under concurrency.
highlights: One-time and time-based share links, public or key-protected and revocable at any moment — several links per note with QR codes and activity logs.
Race-safe view counting with row-level locking and atomic conditional updates in PostgreSQL, proven by a concurrency test against a real server.
Custom server-side sessions (hashed opaque tokens), scrypt password hashing, TOTP two-factor auth with backup codes and remote sign-out.
A local security advisor flags passwords, API keys, card numbers (Luhn) and Aadhaar/PAN before a note is shared.
Optional Gemini features — rewrite, summarise, translate, auto-tags and a “smart share” that suggests safe link settings.
Markdown editor with version history, templates, trash & restore, a command palette and a dashboard with 14-day analytics.

projects.name: 8SpeedyService
projects.tagline: An on-road mechanic in three taps.
projects.summary: An on-demand roadside-mechanic platform for India: a 3-tap customer booking app, a partner-mechanic duty console and a real-time dispatch engine on PostgreSQL.
highlights: Customer app: pick the issue, pick the vehicle (fixed visit fees from ₹149) and book a verified mechanic, with live GPS radar tracking.
Partner app: workshop KYC (ID proof, selfie, shop photo), an online/offline duty switch, 20-second job-offer alerts, 4-digit start-OTP verification and extra-part billing with a 15% ledger.
Two Flutter (Material 3) apps sharing one core package of domain models, theme, REST and Socket.IO clients.
Fastify 5 + PostgreSQL dispatch and ledger service with Socket.IO real-time updates and a Postgres adapter for multi-instance fan-out.
Firebase phone sign-in verified server-side; Helmet, rate limiting, zod validation and integration tests on an embedded PostgreSQL.

projects.name: M-Chat
projects.summary: A multi-agent conversational workspace that routes between Google Gemini, OpenAI and Anthropic models with live web grounding, a two-stage research pipeline and streaming answers — re-architected from my original Python/Streamlit “Mini ChatGPT” into a full-stack TypeScript app.
highlights: Multi-provider model picker with live backend availability checks and bring-your-own-key support.
Adaptive modes: Auto routes between direct chat, live Google Search grounding with citations and Research (Research Agent → Summarizer Agent).
Low-latency NDJSON streaming over Netlify Functions.
Voice dictation, read-aloud, pinned chats, search, multimodal attachments (images, PDFs, text), read-only share links and PDF export.
Input validation, rate limiting, key guards and an adversarial security test suite.

projects.name: WEARSUPER
projects.summary: A full-stack streetwear store — a cinematic GSAP scroll hero, real accounts with bcrypt + JWT, and MongoDB-backed orders with server-side pricing, tracking and cancellation.
highlights: Cinematic hero — a 240-frame image sequence scrubbed by GSAP ScrollTrigger, loaded progressively (a lighter 120-frame set on phones).
Real accounts with bcrypt-hashed passwords and signed JWT sessions behind a rate-limited login.
Orders in MongoDB — the server re-prices every line from the database, validates size and colour and issues order, tracking and invoice numbers.
Order-tracking timeline, printable receipts and cancellation within 20 minutes, enforced by the API.
Product pages with hover-zoom, a drag-to-rotate 360° viewer, reviews, wishlist and a multi-step (simulated) checkout.
API hardened with Helmet, a CORS allow-list and input validation; 17 API tests on an in-memory MongoDB (Node test runner + Supertest).

projects.name: Fresnel
projects.summary: Audits a GitHub repository or a Lighthouse report across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO and light security — then generates ready-to-apply Git commits, unified diffs and a downloadable .patch.
highlights: Static repository audit that never executes untrusted code: LCP prioritisation, render-blocking CSS, CLS image dimensions, WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA checks, CSP, canonical/OG/JSON-LD and DOM-XSS sinks.
Lighthouse JSON analysis that maps failing audits and metric savings back to the templates and stylesheets that caused them.
Interactive diff inspector with per-category commit selection, git format-patch export and a one-click git am + gh pr create command.
Angular 19 standalone components with signals, a Node REST API on Netlify Functions, light/dark themes and a sandbox demo mode.

projects.name: Wizard Chess 3D
projects.summary: A Gothic-cathedral 3D chess game in the browser — sculpted stone pieces, cinematic captures with stone-shatter physics, multiple camera views and a single-player AI opponent.
highlights: Three.js scene with GLB models, orbit controls and player, overhead, side and cathedral camera modes.
Hand-written chess engine with legal-move validation.
Cinematic melee captures with stone-shatter physics.
Play as white or black against an AI opponent — right in the browser, nothing to install.

projects.name: ColorCraft
projects.tagline: Personalised colouring books in a minute.
projects.summary: Turns a theme and a child's name into a personalised five-page story with thick-line Gemini artwork, a digital colouring studio and print-ready PDF export.
highlights: An Express API keeps the Gemini key on the server, with routes for the story plan, page images and chat.
Story planning — Gemini returns a structured five-page storyline with captions and a prompt for every page.
Image generation with an automatic model fallback chain, so a page still renders if one model is unavailable.
Digital colouring studio on HTML5 Canvas, page regeneration with custom prompts and one-click PDF export with jsPDF.

projects.name: Rescuen Web
projects.summary: The official website for Rescuen — passwordless phone-OTP login, a live AI safety assistant, a real contact centre that emails and auto-replies, and a secure serverless backend.
highlights: Passwordless phone → OTP login (Firebase, invisible reCAPTCHA), verified server-side with the Firebase Admin SDK.
AI safety assistant on Google Gemini, running server-side so keys never reach the browser.
Contact centre that emails straight to Gmail and sends the sender an instant branded auto-reply (Nodemailer).
CSP and security headers, rate limiting, zod validation, a honeypot and server-only secrets; full legal and trust pages with JSON-LD.

projects.name: GhoshKart
projects.summary: A multi-page e-commerce site without frameworks — catalogue search and filters, cart, a UPI-style checkout, order tracking and fingerprint/passkey login through WebAuthn.
highlights: Password, PIN and device fingerprint / passkey sign-in through the Web Authentication (WebAuthn) API.
Explore page with search and filters, product pages and a persistent cart.
UPI-style (simulated) checkout and an order history with search and tracking.

projects.name: Cognifyz Internship Suite
projects.tagline: Every internship task, one premium site.
projects.summary: A connected multi-page site housing all three levels of my Cognifyz web-development internship — plus a full scientific calculator and a colour studio.
highlights: Scientific calculator with standard and scientific modes, memory, history, keyboard support and a hand-written tokenizer + shunting-yard evaluator.
Colour Studio with HEX/RGB/HSL sliders, a gradient builder and a palette generator.
Responsive card (Bulma), grid (Bootstrap), media-query layouts, a lightbox gallery with slideshow and a landing page — under one shared design system.

projects.name: Online Examination System
projects.summary: A browser-based exam platform with student and admin portals — timed exams, auto-grading, results and printable grade cards.
highlights: Separate student and admin portals with sign-up and login.
Countdown timer with automatic submission when time runs out.
Automatic grading, a results dashboard and a printable grade card; password-reset and help-desk emails via EmailJS.

projects.name: Face Mask Detection
projects.tagline: Real-time mask detection from a webcam.
projects.summary: OpenCV finds each face in a live webcam feed and a MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model classifies mask / no mask.
highlights: Transfer learning on MobileNetV2 (ImageNet weights) with a custom dense head and data augmentation.
Live inference — Haar-cascade face detection → 224×224 crop → prediction, drawn as a labelled box.

projects.name: CutSlot
projects.tagline: Salon chairs, booked by the slot.
projects.summary: A salon-partner app in Flutter for managing chair availability, time slots and customer bookings.
highlights: Flutter app targeting Android, iOS and desktop from one codebase.

faq.a: Because he ships. Bapan co-built Rescuen and took it live on Google Play, completed two industry internships (Cognifyz, EDU TANTR), and has built {projects} projects — {live} of them live — across web, Android, Fire TV, fintech and AI. His work comes with production habits most freshers skip: tests (184 in Vitrine alone), CSP and rate limits, CI/CD, Docker and Kubernetes. He learns fast and owns things end to end.

faq.q: Is Bapan a fresher? Does he have real experience?
faq.a: He graduates in 2027, so on paper he's a fresher — but not a typical one. He has two completed internships, an app live on the Google Play Store built with a teammate, and production-grade projects with real security, testing and deployment. His projects follow the same habits teams expect in production: tests, CI/CD, security headers, rate limits and real deployments.
Right away for internships — full-time or part-time, remote or on-site. He graduates in June 2027 and is available for full-time SDE roles from then.
Yes. He's based in Bankura, West Bengal and is happy to relocate anywhere in India — Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram/Noida, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata — or to work remotely.
Bapan prefers to discuss compensation directly — he's flexible for the right learning opportunity. You can reach him by email or WhatsApp and he'll respond quickly.

faq.q: What roles is he looking for?
faq.a: SDE / software-engineering internships, full-stack roles (React, Next.js, Angular, Node.js), mobile roles (React Native, Kotlin, Flutter), backend/cloud internships and 2027 new-grad positions.

Yes — data structures and algorithms, OOP, DBMS, operating systems and computer networks are part of his core training, and he practises on LeetCode (BAPAN_GHOSH_07). He also cleared a Data Structures using C assessment from PVG COE Nashik.

faq.q: Can he work in a team?
faq.a: Definitely. Rescuen and Storyloom were both two-person team projects with clear ownership, and his Cognifyz internship certificate specifically commends his dedication, coordination, communication and attention to detail.
For freelance or project work, message Bapan directly by email or WhatsApp with a short brief — he'll get back to you quickly.
Bapan shares academic details on request — his résumé and a quick email are the best way to get them.
